title: Farthest Reach With Wildcard Steps
statement:
A walker starts at position 0 on a number line and follows the instructions in moves one by one. 'L' means step 1 to the left, 'R' means step 1 to the right, and '_' means step 1 in a direction you choose, separately for each '_'.

Return the largest possible distance from 0 at the end of the walk.

examples.why: The fixed steps cancel out: two L and two R. All three wildcards then go the same way.
Send both wildcards right, with the fixed R.
The walker passes 2 on the way, but only the final position counts.

hints: Ignore the wildcards for a moment. Where do the fixed steps leave the walker?
Every wildcard can add 1 to the distance if it points away from 0. Which way is away from 0 after the fixed steps?
Answer = |count('L') − count('R')| + count('_'). If the fixed steps cancel exactly, either direction works.

explain.intuition:
The order of the steps does not matter, only how many go each way, because the final position is just (right steps) − (left steps). So count L, R and _.

The fixed steps leave the walker at R − L. Each wildcard can move one more unit, and the best choice is always to push further from 0 in the direction the walker already leans. That adds every wildcard to the distance: |L − R| + blanks. Splitting the wildcards can only cancel some of them out, never help.
steps: The fixed steps leave the walker |L − R| from 0.
Add the number of wildcards and return the sum.
pitfalls: Tracking the farthest point reached during the walk. Only the final position counts.
Pointing all wildcards right by default. If the walker leans left, they should go left.
Trying every left/right assignment of the wildcards. That is 2<sup>k</sup> work for a one-line answer.

solutions.title: Try both all-left and all-right
solutions.idea: Simulate the walk twice, once with every wildcard as L and once as R, and take the larger final distance.

solutions.title: Count and add
solutions.idea: The fixed steps leave |L − R|; every wildcard adds one more.

followups: Return the farthest distance from 0 reached at any moment during the walk, still choosing the wildcards.
The walk is on a grid with U, D, L, R and wildcards. What is the farthest Manhattan distance?
